Our experiment tested a new multimodal cannabis cue reactivity paradigm that included unimodal pictures, unimodal odors, and bimodal cues combining pictures and odors, and examined whether odor stimuli activated mesocorticolimbic regions to a greater degree than picture stimuli.

description.value: Event-related fMRI paradigm presenting cannabis and flower pictures, odors, and bimodal odor-plus-picture cues, with participants sniffing on every trial.

spans.text: Our experiment tested a new multimodal cannabis cue reactivity paradigm that included unimodal pictures, unimodal odors, and bimodal cues combining pictures and odors

description.value: Participants inhaled a cannabis-like odorant (Cannaroma®, based on the terpene profile of Blue Dream) for 850 ms while viewing the task cue; they were instructed to pause breathing at the yellow cross-hair and inhale through the nose when the green cross-hair appeared.
Participants viewed pictures of cannabis products and paraphernalia for 850 ms while performing the instructed sniff response; no odorant was delivered in this unimodal picture condition.

Participants simultaneously viewed cannabis product/paraphernalia pictures and inhaled the cannabis-like Cannaroma® odorant for 850 ms; they prepared to breathe at the yellow cross-hair and inhaled through the nose at the green cross-hair.
Participants inhaled pure phenylethyl alcohol, a rose-smelling flower odorant, for 850 ms while following the instructed sniff response.

Participants viewed pictures of nonpsychoactive garden-variety flowers and related gardening products for 850 ms while performing the instructed sniff response; no odorant was delivered in this unimodal picture condition.
Participants simultaneously viewed flower/gardening-related pictures and inhaled the rose-smelling phenylethyl alcohol odorant for 850 ms while following the instructed sniff response.

spans.text: We compared brain activation to cannabis cues to a simple baseline condition (i.e., a fixation cross) and to a closely related stimulus type associated with extrinsic reward: flowers.
